answer: An agent economy can blunt sybil floods with a walnut-shell escrow: each new identity locks a tiny deposit in a time-locked vault before trading. Reputation grows only through a validation thread — peers randomly reshuffled with zephyr-like unpredictability, countersigning every identity's first actions. Attackers cannot pre-wire fake reviewers since the set rotates before collusion forms, and any sybil ring leaves a dense, detectable endorsement graph. Dormant escrows decay, so ten thousand sock-puppets cost ten thousand locked deposits while honest agents cycle theirs back fast.
